# 2 Baruch Chapter 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 19:2 — "each one was to himself both an Adam and an Eve"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "each-one-of-them-was-to-himself-both-an-Adam-and-a-Eve" | Literal hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "each one of them was to himself both an Adam and an Eve" | Formal; preserved exactly |
| PNEUMA | "every person was, in their own way, both their own Adam and their own Eve" | Adds "in their own way" and "their own" for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The statement is deliberately paradoxical and striking as written. Adding "in their own way" softens the paradox. The direct "was to himself both an Adam and an Eve" is the theologically precise formulation.

---

## 19:4 — Deut 30:11 quotation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "'The-commandment-which-I-give-you-this-day is-not-too-difficult-for-you, nor-is-it-far-off'" | Literal; preserves hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "'The commandment which I give you this day is not too difficult for you, nor is it far off'" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "'The command I give you today is not too hard for you and it is not out of reach'" | "Command" for "commandment"; "today" for "this day"; "hard" for "difficult" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The formal rendering follows the Syriac Peshitta of Deut 30:11 more closely. "Commandment" over "command" — the Syriac puwqdana is the technical term for divine ordinance.

---

## 19:8 — "love of money" vs. "greed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "out-of-the-love-of-money" | Literal compound |
| LOGOS | "out of the love of money" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "driven by greed" | "Greed" for "love of money" — same referent, different register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Love of money" is the specific Syriac phrase (hubb d'kesp) that parallels 1 Tim 6:10 (philarguria). The specific compound is more precise and has important NT resonance. "Greed" is a broader term.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
